elements.element: Customer is not subject to any exclusivity obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly states that Vendor is “a non-exclusive provider,” and Section 2.1 confirms that Customer may decline to place further orders without breach or shortfall.

elements.element: Customer is not obligated to use Vendor as its sole supplier.
elements.evidence: The original “sole and exclusive provider” language has been replaced with “a non-exclusive provider,” eliminating sole-supplier status.

elements.element: Any exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The fallback requirement is conditional on exclusivity existing. The operative clause demonstrably imposes no exclusivity because Vendor is designated a “non-exclusive provider,” so no broader category exclusivity applies.

elements.element: Any exclusivity is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: The fallback requirement is conditional on exclusivity existing. Because the operative language imposes no exclusivity, Customer cannot be bound by exclusivity beyond 12 months.

elements.element: Any exclusivity ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The fallback requirement is conditional on exclusivity existing. No exclusivity obligation exists, so no service-level failure can leave Customer subject to continuing exclusivity.

elements.element: Any exclusivity ends automatically upon Vendor’s failure to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The fallback requirement is conditional on exclusivity existing. No exclusivity obligation exists, so no delivery-date failure can leave Customer subject to continuing exclusivity.

result.reason: The redline directly removes the sole and exclusive provider obligation and replaces it with an express non-exclusive arrangement. Section 2.1 further confirms that Customer has no minimum purchase or future-order commitment. The change is narrow, introduces no unrelated requirements, and preserves the remaining commercial framework. Because the preferred no-exclusivity position is achieved, the fallback limitations are satisfied as conditional protections whose triggering premise—an exclusivity obligation—is demonstrably absent.
